3	- **R-7vq.** A window’s size and client are its own: the pop-out can show a phone in the mobile app while the surface beside the chat fits the panel, and changing one never changes the other.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
5	  *proposed*
6	- **R-c2m.** The page and the state on show belong to the design, so picking either moves every window showing it.
7	- **R-h9x.** Every design in a project offers the same sizes and clients: the ones its app shell declares, with Fit the panel always first.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design @ typical*
9	- **R-e5n.** A custom size takes a width and a height between 200 and 4000 pixels; anything outside that shows the page fitting the panel.
10	- **R-w3j.** A design remembers one custom size, offered in every window’s size menu after the shell’s sizes; setting another replaces it.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
12	  *proposed*
13	- **R-b6d.** A message may be images alone, with no words.
14	- **R-x8f.** The agent sees every image sent with a message, and the images stay with the session, so they’re still there when it’s opened again.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
16	  *proposed*
17	- **R-m2s.** Only images can be attached (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP); pasting or dropping anything else leaves the message box as it was.
18	- **R-r7h.** Each message tells the agent what the person was looking at when they sent it (the page, the state, and the size and client when they aren’t the defaults), unless they turned that off for it.
19	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design @ typical*
20	- **R-z4k.** Messages sent while the agent is working wait, and go to it together, in the order they were written, when its turn ends.

22	- **R-9cn.** Stopping the agent sends nothing that was waiting: the waiting messages go back into the message box, to send or change.

I built the Pop-out window. Most of it was already done when the Design page was built, so this turn mostly moved the design's view across and recorded the work. Nothing here has run yet; Prelude's render of every route in every state will be the first check.

**What I changed**
- **`server/views/_window.eta`**: replaced with the design's `workspace/window.eta`. The markup is identical; only the comment changed, to name the model (`DesignPage`) and the rule (R-7vq). It uses the surface already in `server/views/_surface.eta`, which matches the design's except where NOTES.md already says the app differs: the real iframe and the design host's log.
- **`routes.json`**: the window route's view is now `@app/server/views/_window`, and its `"from"` is gone.
- **`RULES.md`**: removed the *proposed* lines for R-7vq, R-w3j and R-x8f. Nothing else changed.
- **`NOTES.md`**: the "Built" section now says the pop-out is built, instead of "still to build".

**Already in the app, so no new code was needed**
- **The route** (`server/main.js:1128`): a fragment request gets the window view alone. Otherwise it gets the page in the window layout, with its own live channel (`…/live?view=window`). Opening that channel is how the panel beside the chat knows a window is open and steps aside.
- **R-7vq** (each window keeps its own size and client): they're part of the surface's own address. When the design changes, each window reloads at its own address, so changing one window's size or client never changes the other's.
- **R-w3j** (one remembered custom size): `designs.setCustom` in `server/design-state.js` keeps one custom size per design and replaces it when another is set. Every window lists it after the shell's sizes.
- **R-x8f** (the agent sees sent images, and they stay with the session): sending moves the images into `sessions/<id>/images/` (`server/drafts.js`), and the message tells the agent their paths so it reads them (`promptOf`, `server/main.js:1622`).
- **The two events**: `server/dictation.js` writes the download's progress and its finish, and sends `dictation-changed` each time. The window's channel listens for it.

**Before you approve the screens**
- Compare the Pop-out window in the *popped-out* state with its approved screen. The page should show a real frame where the design draws a placeholder, and the design host's log when there is one; anything else that differs needs a look.
- In the desktop app, pop out, pick Phone in the window, and check that the panel beside the chat stays at Fit the panel. Close the window and check that the panel grows back.
